query: I need help writing a prompt for my team. The idea is to have an AI agent summarize our weekly customer feedback emails into a short digest. Help me get this shaped into something usable.
expect: restates the interpretation in natural language, making assumptions explicit, before asking anything
asks at most one focused question rather than a batched list of questions
does not draft the complete prompt or write a plan document in place of asking

query: I've finished gathering requirements for a prompt I want. Here are my answers: goal — make a coding agent add input validation to our REST API endpoints; in scope — all POST and PUT endpoints, returning 400 with a clear error body; out of scope — GET endpoints, database migrations; assumptions — Python with pydantic already in the project; success criteria — invalid payloads get a 400 and a JSON error body naming the bad field; output format — new validation module plus tests, concise; audience — the coding agent executing it; grounding context — existing `app/routes.py` conventions; failure cases — validation that accepts malformed input, or missing tests. Give me the spec and the final prompt.
expect: the Spec block includes all nine fields: Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Assumptions, Success criteria, Output format, Audience, Grounding context, Failure cases
the complete prompt text is emitted in a single code fence encoding the confirmed fields
the prompt omits few-shot exemplars, chain-of-thought scaffolding, and role personas
does not execute the task (no actual code or validation module is produced)

query: Write me a prompt I can give to a coding agent: add a retry-with-backoff wrapper around all HTTP calls in {RUN_DIR}/api_client.py, retry only on 429 and 5xx, and write a test proving two retries then success. Output just the prompt text.
expect: drafts the prompt directly without conducting a spec interview or asking spec-field questions
does not emit a Spec block for sign-off as a gating step

query: You helped me shape a prompt earlier and you assumed I wanted a prompt for a coding agent to implement the feature. That's wrong — I want a prompt for a product manager to evaluate whether the feature is worth building. Just give me the corrected prompt.
expect: applies the correction directly without restarting a spec interview or asking the spec-field questions again
the emitted prompt is for the corrected goal (evaluation by a product manager), not the original coding-agent implementation
